cc @AxeZhan

Well I was not able to reproduce this on my kind cluster.
@IgorOhrimenko Can you check if you enabled `PodLifecycleSleepAction` feature gate? The errors seems like the feature gate is disabled and the validation fails.
https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/containers/container-lifecycle-hooks/
https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/feature-gates/

@AxeZhan Thanks for your advice. I added the line `    - --feature-gates=PodLifecycleSleepAction=true` into the file `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml` and code:
```yaml
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            sleep:
              seconds: 50
```
applied but does not work but it is another problem.
You need to also add it to kubelet.

Thanks again. Code:
```yaml
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            sleep:
              seconds: 50
```
worked well after I added some instructions on the worker and `systemctl restart kubelet.service`:
1.  `--feature-gates=PodLifecycleSleepAction=true` into `/usr/lib/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-kubeadm.conf`; `systemctl status kubelet.service` shows PodLifecycleSleepAction
2. 
```yaml
featureGates:
  PodLifecycleSleepAction: true
```
into /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml
`systemctl status kubelet.service` does not show PodLifecycleSleepAction

I tried change from master, but kubelet on the exists workers does not read new configs. I found that reinit worker resolve this problem but it is too difficult and low observability if I will use `kubelet.config.k8s.io/v1beta1`. So, I will continue use
```yaml
          lifecycle:
            preStop:
              exec:
                command: ["sleep", "50"]
```
at least until the PodLifecycleSleepAction move to beta and enable by default on all workers.

ftw, there appears to be a bug where applying a Pod manifest with sleep-based preStop hook over an exiting Pod with exec-based preStop hook produces the `Forbidden: may not specify more than 1 handler type` error. Applying the same sleep-based preStop hook manifest over existing Pod without any preStop hooks is error free.

body:
### What happened?

watch connection may be closed when to dispatch bookmark event to all watchers by `dispatchEvent` and when the three condition can be satisfied

if event.Type == watch.Bookmark {

title: QueueingHints(Pod/delete) have to consider that "unassume Pod" is treated as Pod/delete
body:
### What happened?


> Side question: What if the unscheduled Pod was assumed?
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122360#discussion_r1431547953

This question made me wonder what if the Pod was unassumed. 

1. Only one Node which can accomodate only one Pod exists. 
2. Pod-a is assumed to the Node. (but not yet actually bound)
3. Pod-b is rejected because the scheduler assumes Pod-a.
4. Pod-a is somehow unassumed. **It's treated as Pod/delete event.**
5. Pod-a goes to the scheduling queue. Now, the Node has a free space though, will Pod-b be retried? Well, it's depending on the implementation of QHints of Pod/delete...

---

These are plugins that have this problem.

- [ ] nodeports
- [ ] noderesource

For example, nodeports:

> // If the deleted pod is unscheduled, it doesn't make the target pod schedulable.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/42ab3b7b40c34e91b63589ae905ed918752a4a36/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/nodeports/node_ports.go#L136

This is not true, because if the deleted pod is assumed Pod, it makes the target pod schedulable.


### What did you expect to happen?

1. Only one Node which can accomodate only one Pod exists. 
2. Pod-a is assumed to the Node. (but not yet actually bound)
3. Pod-b is rejected because the scheduler assumes Pod-a.
4. Pod-a is somehow unassumed. **It's treated as Pod/delete event.**
5. Pod-a goes to the scheduling queue. **noderesourcefit receives Pod/delete event by (4), and it moves Pod-b to activeQ/backoffQ.**


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The above scenario.

If pod-A anyways goes back to scheduled queue, it does not free up any resources for pod-B. Pod-B will be still unscheduled if we don't consider other changes. Does this "making unassumed" change itself really make it more possible for Pod-B to be scheduled?

> If pod-A anyways goes back to scheduled queue, it does not free up any resources for pod-B.

It does. IIUC, the assumed pod is treated like scheduled pod in the scheduler cache. So, from the scheduler cache pov, "unassume pod from node" is the same as "delete pod that was scheduled on node".

> > If pod-A anyways goes back to scheduled queue, it does not free up any resources for pod-B.
> 
> It does. IIUC, the assumed pod is treated like scheduled pod in the scheduler cache. So, from the scheduler cache pov, "unassume pod from node" is the same as "delete pod that was scheduled on node".

I got what you mean. It frees up more resources only from B's perspective, instead of more resources overall. in the scenario "Only one Node which can accomodate only one Pod exists.", the result will have to be that either A or B are scheduled, instead of both.

Assume you are ahead of another person in a line. You are almost served but the reception wants to pause for a minute. After one minute when it comes back, is it more fair to you to be served immeidately or rebuild the line with another person randomly? I'm not sure which philosophy we prefer generally, but I guess either way should not make difference to the overall efficiency as the overall resources don't change?

> Assume you are ahead of another person in a line. You are almost served but the reception wants to pause for a minute. After one minute when it comes back, is it more fair to you to be served immeidately or rebuild the line with another person randomly? I'm not sure which philosophy we prefer generally, but I guess either way should not make difference to the overall efficiency as the overall resources don't change?

If very simple scenario like the above, Yes.
But, this world is actually much more complicated. There's no guarantee if the receptionist can accommodate me after a minute. One step further scenario:
1. Only one Node with 3 cores exists.
2. Pod-a with 3 cores is assumed to the Node. (but not yet actually bound)
3. Pod-b with 1 core is rejected because the scheduler assumes Pod-a to the Node and the Node has no empty resource.
4. Pod-a is somehow unassumed. It's treated as Pod/delete event.
5. Pod-a goes to the scheduling queue. 
6. Pod-c with 2 cores is scheduled to the Node. 
7. Pod-a comes back to the scheduling cycle, but the Node no longer accepts Pod-a. Pod-a is rejected and put back to the scheduling queue again.
8. Pod-a and Pod-b are in the unschedQ for 5 min (unschedQ timeout). But actually the Node can accommodate Pod-b now.

> This is not true, because if the deleted pod is assumed Pod, it makes the target pod schedulable.

We can take the simple approach and not ignore this change, which would go back to parity with the behavior before scheduling hints.

In general, the deletion of unscheduled pods should be uncommon.
/assign

/close

While implementing the fix, I noticed `assume()` sets an assumed node name to `Pod.Spec.NodeName` internally. So, this bug doesn't exist.

[KEP-1287](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/1287-in-place-update-pod-resources) focus on allowing a running pod resource change to trigger a restart or not. 
- For pending pod without nodeName (during scheduling stage), the KEP doesn't cover. 

I would +1 to decline a resource update  of pending pod, and fix it as a bug. This will reduce complexity of this feature.

BTW, if a pod is not running yet, recreating it with an new resource limit/request is a very low cost operation, the aim of In-Place Update of pod resource to solve running pod resource optimization. We'd better not support pod resource update before scheduled until we have a clear scanerio.
cc @sanposhiho

If a pod is being assumed, the hintFn won't observe update event because the event is filtered by the [updatePodInSchedulingQueue](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/42ab3b7b40c34e91b63589ae905ed918752a4a36/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L132). so we don't need consider this [scenario](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122360#discussion_r1431547953)

@alculquicondor @kerthcet

As @carlory said, assumed Pods' updates are ignored in [updatePodInSchedulingQueue](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/42ab3b7b40c34e91b63589ae905ed918752a4a36/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L132).

And eventually when Pod is bound to some Node, `addPodToCache` is called.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/42ab3b7b40c34e91b63589ae905ed918752a4a36/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L190-L205

Then, what if this scenario happens?↓

1. Pod is assumed to Node-A.
2. Pod is scaled down before Pod is bound to Node-A. updatePodInSchedulingQueue ignores this event.
3. Pod is bound to Node-A. (addPodToCache)

(2) actually makes a free space, but the scheduler ignores it, doesn't it? Could this scenario happen? Is this operation something prohibited by the in-place Pod resizing feature?

> /cc @carlory @vinaykul @thockin [KEP-1287](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/1287-in-place-update-pod-resources) focus on allowing a running pod resource change to trigger a restart or not.
> 
> * For pending pod without nodeName (during scheduling stage), the KEP doesn't cover.
> 
> I would +1 to decline a resource update of pending pod, and fix it as a bug. This will reduce complexity of this feature.
> 
> BTW, if a pod is not running yet, recreating it with an new resource limit/request is a very low cost operation, the aim of In-Place Update of pod resource to solve running pod resource optimization. We'd better not support pod resource update before scheduled until we have a clear scanerio.

+1. Resizing in assumed pods does not provide much value to users, and the feature is still in alpha state so we should be good to make the change.

title: NodeAffinity/NodeUnschedulable QueueingHint may miss Node related events that make Pod schedulable
body:
### What happened?

/kind bug
/triage accepted
/priority urgent
/sig scheduling
/assign

NodeAffinity QueueingHint may miss Node related events that make Pod schedulable because of preCheck.
It's similar to: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119177#issuecomment-1820091877

So:
1. Node is added. But, it's filtered out by preCheck (due to node's unready or whatever) and the scheduling queue doesn't receive NodeAdded. (noderesourcefit cannot receive NodeAdded.)
2. Node is updated and ready now. But, this event is NodeUpdated.

In such scenarios, NodeAffinity may return `QueueSkip` to the event due to (2).
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/nodeaffinity/node_affinity.go#L94-L131

### What did you expect to happen?

We have to loosen the filtering in `isSchedulableAfterNodeChange` until preCheck is removed.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/110175

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a Pod with NodeAffinity under the situation where no Node can accommodate the Pod.
2. Create a new Node.

It may cause the above problematic scenario.

Yes, I just went through all, and seems these two are the only ones that has got QHint in the last release.

Other QHints:

- NodePort 🙆‍♂️  https://github.com/sanposhiho/kubernetes/blob/7cba35f6519c6e0cf72848185ef3f9a524601467/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/nodeports/node_ports.go#L118-L124
- DRA: doesn't have QHint for Node events

Wait... I think https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109437 has been silently coming back since it's closed. (We should have mentioned it in the comment somewhere...)
Regardless of whether QHint is implemented or not, we have to make sure all plugins that have Node Add event to have Node Update event. I see some plugins don't follow it. (we must mention it in the doc somewhere.)
If you mean the newly added plugins like the DRA, I think yes, let me check that in.

Yes, I meant that. For newly added plugins like DRA, they have NodeAdd, but not NodeUpdated.
I haven't checked all, but NodeUnschedulable is also the one that reverting QHint is not enough, but adding Node Update event is necessary to be added to completely fix the issue.

We discussed at slack:
https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C2C40FMNF/p1702438650646789

And decided we'll make the feature gate for QHint disable by default. (There was a discussion of disablement for this before actually because we observed a memory consumption issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120622) This issue reinforces that idea. We'll make it enable by default once all issues here + memory consumption issue are addressed.
Also, one general problem is that we have few integration (or e2e) tests for requeueing scenario.

Related problems we faced now: 
1. preCheck has some potential bugs as https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/110175 described, so we're planning to remove preCheck someday(without obvious performance degradation)
2. currently, node related plugins like `nodeUnschedulable` & `nodeAffinity` & `nodeResourceFit` with tight validations in hintFunc is conflict with preCheck as this issue mentioned.
3. Also because of preCheck, node plugins register `nodeAdd` events should also register the `nodeUpdate` event, DRA  is one plugin we missed. (I'll raise a quick fix with the consistent policy we applied now)

To the 2nd question, a feasible approach is only check the newObj (we're now validating the oldObj and newObj both, only the oldObj doesn't match but the newObj does, then we'll return `Queue`), still better than before when we only watch for the event. But the disadvantage is not that efficient, like we have two plugins A & B, also two nodes Node1, Node2. When pod is scheduling, Node1 is failed by pluginA, Node2 is failed by pluginB, so when Node2 updated, pluginA will pass the validation however, pod is still unschedulable.

Regarding (3), what do you think about this idea: when plugins register `nodeAdd`, we automatically register `nodeUpdated` (until preCheck is removed) so that we could technically prevent https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109437 happening again in any plugins (including both in-tree and external).

The action items in my mind (correct me if I am mistaken or missed something.)

- [ ] plugins that have `nodeAdd` should have `nodeUpdate` as well. (maybe we'll fix it via https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122292)
- [ ] revert PRs of NodeAffinity/NodeUnschedulable QHints (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122285 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122288) and cherry-pick them.

title: Follow up #121985: Conformance test regarding the access of "/"
body:
### What happened?

The issue is to follow up discussions in #121985: running conformance test with the commonly used tool, sonobuoy, failed because the tool's test runner is lack of permission towards `/`. The original issue was resolved by changing the e2e (conformance) test of `/` to an integration test. Several problems remained:

1. The privilege requirement in [conformance-tests.md](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/conformance-tests.md) is outdated. 
    > it is non-privileged (e.g., does not require root on nodes, access to raw network interfaces, or cluster admin permissions)
2. Root discovery is one of the least-privileged permissions, and is expected to be granted to every authenticated user but is not actually.
3. Should the result returned by `/` should be part of conformance?

1st and 2nd are straightforward to fix, not sure about 3rd, should we add a separate test or add a verification step in existing one like https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121283? With the fix of 2nd, e2e for `/` should no longer fail with any test runner.


cc @liggitt @sttts @BenTheElder @neolit123 @aojea 

### What did you expect to happen?

1. conformance-tests.md should be reflect the accurate permission requirement
2. Root discovery permission should be granted to all authenticated users.
3. Conformance test should check the result returned by `/`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I agree with this. We have conformance tests around things like webhooks and custom resource definitions. I'd recommend rephrasing that as "limits itself to capabilities exposed via APIs (e.g., does not require root on nodes, access to raw network interfaces) and does not require write access to system namespaces (like kube-system)"

> Root discovery is one of the least-privileged permissions, and is expected to be granted to every authenticated user but is not actually.

I'm not sure I agree with this. No binaries Kubernetes provides (that I'm aware of) and nothing in client-go needs to make use of root discovery information. I'd be very slow to expand endpoints included in `system:discovery`.

> Should the result returned by / should be part of conformance?

Unless we have compelling reasons for people to use and rely on this data, I would lean towards no.

title: service-account-token falsely reported as created when there is not service-account
body:
### What happened?

While creating the secret with `type: kubernetes.io/service-account-token` it is reported as created:

```
$ kubectl  apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: my-secret
  annotations:
    kubernetes.io/service-account.name: my-sa
type: kubernetes.io/service-account-token
EOF

> secret/my-secret created
```

but it is actually not created until there is a corresponding service-account existing:

```
$ kubectl get sa my-sa
Error from server (NotFound): serviceaccounts "my-sa" not found

$ kubectl get secrets --all-namespaces
No resources found
```

> On the recreation (`kubectl apply`) of the secret it is once again reported as `created`

### What did you expect to happen?

The secret should not be reported as created, or there should be a warning that it won't be visible until the `service-account` exists/

On the recreation (running `kubectl apply` again ) of the secret it is once again reported as `created` instead of expected `unchanged`/`updated`

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

execute:

```
kubectl  apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: my-secret
  annotations:
    kubernetes.io/service-account.name: not-existing-service-account
type: kubernetes.io/service-account-token
EOF
```

and after:
```
secret/my-secret created
```
check if it is visible/exists with `kubectl get secrets`

title: Scheduler's default plugin returns an invalid score that is not in the range of [0, 100], resulting in no Pods being scheduled
body:
### What happened?

Scheduler's default plugin returns an invalid score that is not in the range of [0, 100], resulting in no Pods being scheduled:
```
E1127 19:48:13.221979   66549 schedule_one.go:130] "Error selecting node for pod" err="applying score defaultWeights on Score plugins: plugin \"PodTopologySpread\" returns an invalid score 300, it should in the range of [0, 100] after normalizing" pod="default/test-multi-point-xxxxxxxx"
```

After investigation, I found that there was a bug in the code that built the framework when the scheduler started. When using the plugins declared in the regular extension point to override the plugins declared in the MultiPoint, the traversed variable `enabledSet` will be modified in the following loop:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ad9b60e2c9ddb21e8b00cabbe27e639638a0ea88/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L523-L534

This may cause **a same scoring plugin** (e.g. `PodTopologySpread`) **to be loaded multiple times**:
```
f.scorePlugins: []framework.ScorePlugin{(*noderesources.Fit)(0xc000922e10), (*podtopologyspread.PodTopologySpread)(0xc0000ab100), (*podtopologyspread.PodTopologySpread)(0xc0000ab100), (*tainttoleration.TaintToleration)(0xc0003f3690), (*nodeaffinity.NodeAffinity)(0xc0003997a0), (*volumebinding.VolumeBinding)(0xc0003db7a0), (*interpodaffinity.InterPodAffinity)(0xc00038f3b0), (*noderesources.BalancedAllocation)(0xc000063680), (*imagelocality.ImageLocality)(0xc000b45320)}
```

Further, this results in **a node being processed multiple times by a plugin's** (e.g. `PodTopologySpread`'s) **`NormalizeScore` method**, resulting in an invalid score that is not in the range of [0, 100]:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ad9b60e2c9ddb21e8b00cabbe27e639638a0ea88/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L1095-L1108

### What did you expect to happen?

If the scheduler's MultiPoint feature is used (either through the default plugins or through manual configuration), and the configuration (e.g. the scoring weight) of a certain plugin is overridden in a regular extension point, the plugin will only be loaded once in this extension point, and no illegal scores will be returned.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

An example KubeSchedulerConfiguration:

```yaml
apiVersion: kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1beta3
...
profiles:
- schedulerName: default-scheduler
  plugins:
    score:
      enabled:
      - name: PodTopologySpread
        weight: 3
...
```

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

K8s v1.24.15 or higher


### Cloud provider

None

$ cat /etc/os-release

title: No proper scheduling retries could be made when Extender filters out some Nodes
body:
### What happened?

When Extender filters out some Nodes, we don't set any unschedulable plugins at all. It means Extender is completely ignored during the requeueing process.

So, what's happening is:
- If Extender filters out all Nodes during scheduling, this Pod is soon retried because this Pod doesn't have any plugin name in unschedulable plugins.
- If Extender filters out some Nodes during scheduling and plugins filter out all other Nodes, this Pod is retried based on plugins' QueueingHint. Even if any cluster events happen and it could change Extender's decision (but not any plugins' decision), this Pod won't be requeued to activeQ/backoffQ.

The latter case is serious because it could make Pods being stuck in unschedulable pod pool in 5min.

### What did you expect to happen?

We should have a short-term solution for the latter case. 
We can requeue Pods, which were rejected by Extender, by any kind of cluster events because we cannot know which events make Pods schedulable.

Eventually, this issue makes us wonder how Pods rejected by Extender should be requeued. We cannot implement QHint equivalent in Extenders because it'd be too slow to call Extender every time any cluster events happen. Probably, somehow implementing EventsToRegister equivalent in Extender? 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Use Extender which does something in Filter.

-->

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

<!--
Add one of the following kinds:
/kind bug
/kind cleanup
/kind documentation
/kind feature

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change
/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test
/kind flake
/kind regression
-->

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Extender doesn't support any kind of requeueing feature like EnqueueExtensions in the scheduling framework.

When Extender filters out some Nodes, we don't set any unschedulable plugins at all. 
It means Extender is completely ignored during the requeueing process.

So, what's happening is:
- If Extender filters out all Nodes during scheduling, this Pod is soon retried because this Pod doesn't have any plugin name in unschedulable plugins. The scheduling queue doesn't put this Pod into the unschedulable pod pool, but put into activeQ/backoffQ.
- If Extender filters out some Nodes and plugins filter out all other Nodes, this Pod is retried based on plugins' QueueingHint. Even if some cluster events happen and they could change Extender's decision, this Pod won't be requeued to activeQ/backoffQ.

The latter case is serious because it could make Pods stuck in unschedulable pod pool in 5min in the worst case scenario.

This PR makes the scheduling queue aware of extenders' failures.
After this PR, when Extenders reject some Nodes and the pod ends up being unschedulable, this Pod will be requeued from unschedulable pod pool to activeQ/backoffQ by any kind of cluster events.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

title: One service manages multiple deployment instances. Service uses nodePort type. Upstream traffic is distributed unevenly through different deployment through nodePort.
body:
### What happened? Due to business requirements, a single Service is needed to manage multiple deployments for a simple grayscale scheme. When I associated a deployment tag change to an existing Service, I found that the traffic was skewed. Traffic access path: nginx --> Service nodePort --> deployment1 |--> deployment2 ### What did you expect to happen? It was found that when grayscale a new deployment pod, severe traffic skew occurred. ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? Recurrence scheme first run with deployment-1, the traffic is load balanced, but when deployment-2 is enabled, the traffic will tilt. Why don't you use an Ingress?

> Why don't you use an Ingress?

For some historical reasons, the ingress version of this cluster is older than 0.32 and cannot better support returning to the original IP, so this service uses the nodePort method

> first run with deployment-1, the traffic is load balanced, but when deployment-2 is enabled, the traffic will tilt.

[keepalive](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_upstream_module.html#keepalive) maintains connection cache, reuses same TCP sockets .. so it is possible when deployment-2 is rolled out nginx is still using old/open TCP connections (deployment-1) causing a skew in traffic. 

 

> for i in `seq 1 10000`;do sleep 1 ; curl -s  http://10.4.83.27:8081/ ;done

Also noticed you are running this sequentially, load-balancing won't be of much use here as nignx will try its best to use any existing/open TCP connection as part of optimisation. 

Can you run this in parallel and check if skewness still presists ?

> > first run with deployment-1, the traffic is load balanced, but when deployment-2 is enabled, the traffic will tilt.
> 
> [keepalive](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_upstream_module.html#keepalive) maintains connection cache, reuses same TCP sockets .. so it is possible when deployment-2 is rolled out nginx is still using old/open TCP connections (deployment-1) causing a skew in traffic.

First of all, thank you for your enthusiastic reply. 
Long connections may cause traffic skew, but this problem seems to be extreme. Using an actual business instance to reproduce, almost all the traffic will be sent to the new grayscale instance, causing the new instance to The request volume is too high to respond.

In addition, I tried concurrent access, and the problem still exists. Testing process:
```
time seq 1 2000 | parallel -j5 curl -s "http://10.4.83.27:8081/" >> /tmp/2000.txt

cat /tmp/2000.txt | grep 'http-deployment-1' | wc -l
1590
cat /tmp/2000.txt | grep 'http-deployment-2' | wc -l
410
```
> The reproduction plan is a bit crude. This problem is an actual production gateway instance. The normal Qps is 300/s. After grayscale, there is a serious traffic skew.

In the upstream backend (nginx) you are setting keepalive to 300 and in the concurrent load-test the concurrency is 5. 

I think load-test concurrency should be greater than the number of keepalive connections.

K8s v1.17.16 is not supported (it's super-old!), and _a lot_ has changed, for instance endpoints->endpointslices, which is likely relevant in this case.

I will try to re-create this on v1.28.4 with a different but similar setup:
1. Create a deployment and a service with nodePort
2. Verify distribution from external clients
3. Add another deployment with the same selector, and same "replicas"
4. Check if the new deployment gets a too-large share of new connections

All connections are closed between the tests, and client (src) addresses will be different

### What happened?

The following tests are currently being passed. However, the correct name should be "nodes", not "node".
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ec5096fa869b801d6eb1bf019819287ca61edc4d/pkg/scheduler/scheduler_test.go#L328-L352

Fixing this will lead to the test failing.
```diff
$ git diff
diff --git a/pkg/scheduler/scheduler_test.go b/pkg/scheduler/scheduler_test.go
index b346046610b..e88d0030665 100644
--- a/pkg/scheduler/scheduler_test.go
+++ b/pkg/scheduler/scheduler_test.go
@@ -340,13 +340,13 @@ func TestFailureHandler_NodeNotFound(t *testing.T) {
                        name:             "node is deleted during a scheduling cycle",
                        nodes:            []v1.Node{*nodeFoo, *nodeBar},
                        nodeNameToDelete: "foo",
-                       injectErr:        apierrors.NewNotFound(v1.Resource("node"), nodeFoo.Name),
+                       injectErr:        apierrors.NewNotFound(v1.Resource("nodes"), nodeFoo.Name),
                        expectNodeNames:  sets.New("bar"),
                },
                {
                        name:            "node is not deleted but NodeNotFound is received incorrectly",
                        nodes:           []v1.Node{*nodeFoo, *nodeBar},
-                       injectErr:       apierrors.NewNotFound(v1.Resource("node"), nodeFoo.Name),
+                       injectErr:       apierrors.NewNotFound(v1.Resource("nodes"), nodeFoo.Name),
                        expectNodeNames: sets.New("foo", "bar"),
                },
        }
```

```console
$ go test -run 'TestFailureHandler_NodeNotFound$' ./pkg/scheduler
--- FAIL: TestFailureHandler_NodeNotFound (0.00s)
    --- FAIL: TestFailureHandler_NodeNotFound/node_is_deleted_during_a_scheduling_cycle (0.00s)
        node_tree.go:65: I1121 21:14:35.137431] Added node in listed group to NodeTree node="foo" zone=""
        node_tree.go:65: I1121 21:14:35.137476] Added node in listed group to NodeTree node="bar" zone=""
        schedule_one.go:989: I1121 21:14:35.137547] Unable to schedule pod, possibly due to node not found; waiting pod="default/test-pod" err="nodes \"foo\" not found"
        scheduling_queue.go:655: I1121 21:14:35.137572] Checking events for in-flight pod pod="default/test-pod" unschedulablePlugins=null inFlightEventsSize=0 inFlightPodsSize=0
        scheduling_queue.go:797: I1121 21:14:35.137584] Pod moved to an internal scheduling queue pod="default/test-pod" event="ScheduleAttemptFailure" queue="Unschedulable" schedulingCycle=0 hint=0 unschedulable plugins={}
        schedule_one.go:1068: I1121 21:14:35.137604] Updating pod condition pod="default/test-pod" conditionType="PodScheduled" conditionStatus="False" conditionReason="Unschedulable"
        scheduler_test.go:392: Unexpected nodes (-want, +got):   sets.Set[string](
            -   {"bar": {}},
            +   {"bar": {}, "foo": {}},
              )
FAIL
FAIL    k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/scheduler 0.039s
FAIL
```

Perhaps the cause is here.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ec5096fa869b801d6eb1bf019819287ca61edc4d/pkg/scheduler/schedule_one.go#L990

Pass the unit test.

title: Minimize ensuring kube chains and jump rules
body:
### What happened? IPVS proxier currently ensures kube-chains and jump rules on ever sync loop. These calls are expensive and consumes roughly 32% of CPU time of the sync loop. IPTables doesn't ensure the jump chains on every sync loop. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114181. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/8509ab82b96caa2365552efa08c8ba8baf11c5ec/pkg/proxy/ipvs/proxier.go#L1744-L1765 ### What did you expect to happen? Ensure chain/rules should not happen on every sync call. This only happens in IPTables if `proxier.needFullSync is true` which was introduced during `MinimizeIPTablesRestore` but as this feature got graduated there is no way to disable it. Maybe we can have the IPVS backend behave similarly ... or introduce a new feature to gate it ? sig/network area/ipvs cc. @uablrek ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? This happens on every sync loop. ### Anything else we need to know? _No response_ ### Kubernetes version

title: Trafic to externalIps of service with externalTrafficPolicy=Local and type=LoadBalancer is rejected from local pods.
body:
### What happened?

I have a Service in v1.27.5 k8s version:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
status:
  loadBalancer:
    ingress:
      - ip: 10.3.49.15
spec:
  ports:
    - name: http
      protocol: TCP
      port: 80
      targetPort: http
  selector:
    ...
  clusterIP: 10.233.49.242
  clusterIPs:
    - 10.233.49.242
  type: LoadBalancer
  externalIPs:
    - 10.3.49.15
    - 10.3.49.16
  sessionAffinity: None
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local
  healthCheckNodePort: 32699
  ipFamilies:
    - IPv4
  ipFamilyPolicy: SingleStack
  allocateLoadBalancerNodePorts: true
  internalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
```

I have 2 pods on the node with CNI IPs (calico). One pod (nginx) matches labelSelector of the service.
I make a curl request from the second pod:

```
# curl 10.3.49.15
default backend - 404

# curl 10.3.49.16
curl: (7) Failed to connect to 10.49.1.125 port 80 after 0 ms: Couldn't connect to server
```

First request is successful. The second request is rejected with icmp-port-unreachable.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect both of the requests are successfull (as in the v1.24.6 version).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a Service with my configuration and two pods. Make two requests: 

1. to ip placed both to status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].ip and externalIPs
2. to ip placed only in externalIPs

### Anything else we need to know?

I see that ip 10.3.49.15 is placed to ipsets:

1. KUBE-EXTERNAL-IP-LOCAL
2. KUBE-IPVS-IPS
3. KUBE-LOAD-BALANCER
4. KUBE-LOAD-BALANCER-LOCAL

And 10.3.49.16 is placed to ipsets:

1. KUBE-EXTERNAL-IP-LOCAL
2. KUBE-IPVS-IPS

And iptables rules rejects the trafic to the second address:

```
-A KUBE-IPVS-FILTER -m set --match-set KUBE-LOAD-BALANCER dst,dst -j RETURN
-A KUBE-IPVS-FILTER -m set --match-set KUBE-CLUSTER-IP dst,dst -j RETURN
-A KUBE-IPVS-FILTER -m set --match-set KUBE-EXTERNAL-IP dst,dst -j RETURN
-A KUBE-IPVS-FILTER -m set --match-set KUBE-HEALTH-CHECK-NODE-PORT dst -j RETURN
-A KUBE-IPVS-FILTER -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m set --match-set KUBE-IPVS-IPS dst -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable
```

I think, the ips must be placed both to KUBE-EXTERNAL-IP-LOCAL and KUBE-EXTERNAL-IP ipsets.

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
$ kubectl version

Client Version: v1.28.2
Kustomize Version: v5.0.4-0.20230601165947-6ce0bf390ce3
Server Version: v1.27.5
```

title: Secrets managedFields do not get updated when Secret data is updated via `kubectl edit`
body:
### What happened?

The `managedFields` map of `Secrets` do not get updated when using `kubectl edit` to update Secret `data`

This might be related to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109576 but it is specifically for kind `Secrets`, while  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109576 refers to `ConfigMap`

I am not sure if this is the expected behaviour, but this is something we would like to know, since we have an operator that triggers a Deploy template patch when Secrets referenced by the Deployment gets updated. 

The `kubectl edit` should be a rare use-case, since we normally update Secrets via CI/CD pipelines (patching), but for non-prod environments we might interact with Secrets directly (i.e. using `kubectl edit`). 

Unfortunately I cannot find any clear documentation about this. It would be good to know if this is the expected behaviour so that we should always update the Secret using `patch` OR if this is a bug. Thank you.

References:

* https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/server-side-apply/#field-management
* https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/common-definitions/object-meta/#System


### What did you expect to happen?

`managedFields` of `Secrets` to get updated after running `kubectl edit`

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This is a quick test to reproduce. Note the last timestamp after each test.

```bash
# create Secret 1
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
data:
  s: c29tCg==
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: "1"
  namespace: default
type: Opaque
EOF
secret/1 created
$ kubectl get secret 1 --show-managed-fields -o jsonpath='{range .metadata.managedFields[*]}{.manager}{" did "}{.operation}{" at "}{.time}{"\n"}{end}'
kubectl-client-side-apply did Update at 2023-11-13T10:44:59Z

# test Secret 1 patch
$ kubectl patch secret 1 -p '{"data": {"s": "cHBwCg=="}}'
secret/1 patched
$ kubectl get secret 1 --show-managed-fields -o jsonpath='{range .metadata.managedFields[*]}{.manager}{" did "}{.operation}{" at "}{.time}{"\n"}{end}'
kubectl-client-side-apply did Update at 2023-11-13T10:44:59Z
kubectl-patch did Update at 2023-11-13T10:45:44Z

# test Secret 1 edit
$ k edit secret 1
secret/1 edited
$ kubectl get secret 1 --show-managed-fields -o jsonpath='{range .metadata.managedFields[*]}{.manager}{" did "}{.operation}{" at "}{.time}{"\n"}{end}'
kubectl-client-side-apply did Update at 2023-11-13T10:44:59Z
kubectl-edit did Update at 2023-11-13T10:48:01Z

# edit Secret 1 again
$ k edit secret 1
secret/1 edited
$ kubectl get secret 1 --show-managed-fields -o jsonpath='{range .metadata.managedFields[*]}{.manager}{" did "}{.operation}{" at "}{.time}{"\n"}{end}'
kubectl-client-side-apply did Update at 2023-11-13T10:44:59Z
kubectl-edit did Update at 2023-11-13T10:48:01Z

# the second Secret 1 edit did not trigger the managedFields update
```

title: Does noderestriction also need to be extended for node references in tokens?
body:
### What happened?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120780 recently merged, adding nodes as something we can put in bound object refs (yay!)

Today while reading noderestriction code for a different reason, I realized we never extended noderestriction to block Kubelets from binding tokens to nodes other than themselves. Today, noderestriction _does_ block Kubelets from binding tokens to Pods on other nodes, so perhaps it should do the same for bound node references. 



### What did you expect to happen?

noderestriction to block it, probably.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Read the code here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/263ab254ef6a847fdd3dc69250a2ac0b12c42eb3/plugin/pkg/admission/noderestriction/admission.go#L531-L570

And note that we didn't modify noderestriction.go in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120780/files

To summarize Slack discussion: https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C0EN96KUY/p1699051321839849

- TokenRequest can only bind to one object at a time.
- kubelet (node identity) is already required to bind to Pod by noderestriction. 
- kube-apiserver automatically inserts the node information based on the Pod binding. kubelet does not set it.

So this is technically still node bound.

We should still add a comment in noderestriction.go to avoid future confusion.

There may be other reasons to add a check, like future proofing...

title: endpoints not configured with MinimizeIPTablesRestore
body:
### What happened?

To test out the MinimizeIPTablesRestore feature enabled in 1.27 by default we enabled the setting in 1.26 and discovered that it appears to not configure endpoints properly everytime.
While the version in 1.26 is still alpha I have not found any significant changes, bug reports or backports in the changelog regarding this.

It seems sometimes kube-proxy does not see that the endpoints of a service need to be updated despite the api endpointslice having changed. This typically is not that visible with externalTrafficPolicy Cluster services as some other endpoint still is configured, but in the case of low replica services or externalTrafficPolicy Local services this can lead to service disruption due to the only endpoint on the local node not getting configured while other components see the update correctly and direct traffic there.


For example this two pod deployment both pods ready since hours:

```
$ kubectl -n ns get pods pod1 pod2-o yaml | grep -B 2 Ready
      lastTransitionTime: "2023-10-19T10:21:19Z"
      status: "True"
      type: Ready
--
      lastTransitionTime: "2023-10-19T10:21:19Z"
      status: "True"
      type: ContainersReady
--
      lastTransitionTime: "2023-10-19T10:20:19Z"
      status: "True"
      type: Ready
--
      lastTransitionTime: "2023-10-19T10:20:19Z"
      status: "True"
      type: ContainersReady

```

and the chain on one node only contains one of the ready endpoints:

```
KUBE-SERVICES -d 10.78.44.163/32 -p tcp -m comment --comment "svc:serviceport loadbalancer IP" -m tcp --dport 4000 -j KUBE-EXT-APW7J2FZSAAP4Z43
KUBE-EXT-APW7J2FZSAAP4Z43 -m comment --comment "masquerade traffic for svc:serviceport external destinations" -j KUBE-MARK-MASQ
KUBE-EXT-APW7J2FZSAAP4Z43 -j KUBE-SVC-APW7J2FZSAAP4Z43
KUBE-SVC-APW7J2FZSAAP4Z43 ! -s 100.64.0.0/13 -d 100.72.16.186/32 -p tcp -m comment --comment "svc:serviceport cluster IP" -m tcp --dport 4000 -j KUBE-MARK-MASQ
KUBE-SVC-APW7J2FZSAAP4Z43 -j KUBE-SEP-JDEM23RCGZCIYUJI

KUBE-SEP-JDEM23RCGZCIYUJI -p tcp -m tcp -j DNAT --to-destination 100.64.131.130:4000
```

this situation remains until either the pod readiness changes, a partial sync fails and it does a full resync or kube-proxy is restartet which also full syncs

The kube-proxy logs show nothing unusual, just lots of partial syncs (which in our cluster take about 1-2 seconds for a partial sync while the full sync takes 20-40seconds).

### What did you expect to happen?

On endpoint change the iptables are always configured.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

We see this in clusters with 1500 services, 14000 pods and 300 nodes on most nodes for a small handful of the services.
The cluster is running v1.26.9
I have written a very crude script to check for the inconsistencies and fix them via a proxy restart:
https://gist.github.com/juliantaylor/996e0255809cb2077b66dc034ec47f55

Note due to races it can report errors while stuff in the cluster is changing, but if a deployment behind an ip is stable and still shows up kube-proxy has not configured it properly. (One could at a check on the ready state transition time in the script to avoid this)

and ends there, missing is the jump to the SVL chain (added after restart):

```

KUBE-EXT-O5TNKVKDWS2IHWWC -j KUBE-SVL-O5TNKVKDWS2IHWWC
```

what is interesting is that the "has no local endpoints" DROP rule is also _not_ added, as that is generated from the full endpoint set and also always written in partial writes and `hasExternalEndpoints` is true.

This imo indicates a problem with the `endpointsChanged` function:


```
if tryPartialSync && !serviceChanged.Has(svcName.NamespacedName.String()) && !endpointsChanged.Has(svcName.NamespacedName.String()) {
```

/sig network
/area kube-proxy
/cc @danwinship

/assign

> a partial sync fails and it does a full resync

Is that happening a lot? It shouldn't...

> /assign
> 
> > a partial sync fails and it does a full resync

not a lot, during high cluster activity of  O(10) endpoint changes per second about 0.1/s total on 300 node cluster but that is not the problem here, just one of the ways a full sync is triggered which fixes the missing endpoints.

@juliantaylor I think that can be useful if you increase the logging in the kube-proxy and you print timestamps in your script and upload:
-  kube-proxy logs with verbosity -v4
-  output of your script with timestamps
-  one of the problematic iptables dumps

the iptables snipped I pasted for the Local service is the main part, no jump to the local chain, no local chain and notably no "no local endpoints" DROP. Just the cluster chain is not included but that's just a bunch of endpoints with the local one also missing, but I can provide the full thing for the service next week.

timestamps in the script comparing endpoints to existing iptables configuration are not relevant as its a persistent situation, once it did not configure an endpoint this will not change until something triggers a new endpoint change on the service or it does a full sync. The script can be run at any time and it reports inconsistent configuration.

don't see any interesting logging in the related code of kube-proxy (based on the missing DROP proxier is probably fine and the issue is likely in the EndpointsChangeTracker) but I'll see what I can do.
let me rephrase, it will be important to correlate the partial syncs with the update events and the failures to see if that can give us a hint on why the reconcile loop omits that chain,

> no jump to the local chain, no local chain and notably no "no local endpoints" DROP.

right; the EXT chain is stale. At some point in time there are actually no endpoints, and it writes out a DROP rule and an EXT chain with no jump to the SVL chain. Then an endpoint appears, and it removes the DROP rule but for some reason _doesn't_ rewrite the EXT chain.

> > no jump to the local chain, no local chain and notably no "no local endpoints" DROP.
> 
> right; the EXT chain is stale. At some point in time there are actually no endpoints, and it writes out a DROP rule and an EXT chain with no jump to the SVL chain. Then an endpoint appears, and it removes the DROP rule but for some reason _doesn't_ rewrite the EXT chain.

exactly, the reason for that is that the DROP rule is part of the code that is always rewritten, but the EXT chain is skipped if it thinks nothing changed https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L1200
so the `allEndpoints` is filled correctly it sets `hasExternalEndpoints=true` and it removes the DROP rule, but then `endpoints.Changed` from `pendingChanges` is false and it skips writing the local chain.

this is not specific to the local chains, cluster chains have the same problem, just those are less noticeable as couple nodes missing some endpoints seldom has observable effect.

> This imo indicates a problem with the `endpointsChanged` function:

(`endpointsChanged` is a set; the function there is just `endpointsChanged.Has()`. So the problem would be "a problem with the contents of the `endpointsChanged` set".)

OK, so here are my thoughts so far...

1. If there's a bug in `EndpointsChangeTracker.PendingChanges()`, such that `endpointsChanged` ends up not including some changed endpoints despite the tracker having noticed that they changed and triggering a resync, then we'd fail to rewrite the rules for those endpoints. Alternatively, the same could be true for `ServiceChangeTracker.PendingChanges()`/`servicesChanged`.
    - This seems unlikely: the logic for deciding what's in `endpointsChanged`/`servicesChanged` is pretty closely tied to the logic for triggering syncs. It seems like if the tracker noticed the change at all, it ought to show up in `endpointsChanged`/`servicesChanged`. Or at least, if there _was_ a bug here, it ought to be pretty obvious, not something rare/subtle.
2. If there's a bug in `EndpointsChangeTracker` more generally such that it fails to trigger syncs on some EndpointSlice changes, then the endpoint also wouldn't show up in `endpointsChanged` and so we wouldn't rewrite its chains. (Or again, the problem could be with `ServiceChangeTracker` rather than `EndpointsChangeTracker`.)
    - In this case there would have been a bug even in the pre-MinimizeIPTablesRestore behavior, but it's possible we just never noticed it, since _any_ later change would pick up the previously-ignored Service/EndpointSlice change as well, so the effect would only be that the update was slightly delayed, not missed entirely.
    - If there was a missing mutex lock somewhere then there could be a data race that causes an update to be missed?
3. If set of "usable" endpoints for a Service (i.e., one of the return values of `CategorizeEndpoints`) changes without the Service itself or any of its EndpointSlices having changed (in a relevant way), then we might need to rewrite the service/endpoint chains but not do so.
    - e.g., if either (a) `hasEndpoints` changed from `false` to `true`, or (b) `localEndpoints` changed from empty to non-empty, _without_ `servicesChanged` or `endpointsChanged` including the service, then we would end up with the set of rules you quoted above.
    - At first I was thinking that must be it, but after looking at the code some more, I don't think that can actually happen...
      - The return values of `CategorizeEndpoints` will change for a Cluster policy service if the result of `canUseTopology()` changes, but that can only change if either (a) the service changes (in which case it should be in `servicesChanged`), (b) at least one endpoint changes (in which case it should be in `endpointsChanged`), or (c) the node labels change (in which case `OnNodeUpdate` would force a full resync).
      - The return values of `CategorizeEndpoints` can change when a service flips between using Ready endpoints and using Serving-Terminating endpoints. e.g., if endpoint A is Local,Ready, and endpoint B is Local,Serving,Terminating, then the returned `localEndpoints` would be `[A]`. If endpoint A then terminates, then `localEndpoints` would change to `[A, B]` _even though B didn't change_. But that shouldn't actually cause any problems, because `endpointsChanged` tracks whether _any_ endpoint for the service changed, and in this case A changed, so we should be ok.

I'm leaning toward (2), though (3) still worries me...

but how can we get more nat rules with the same number of Services and less Endpoints?

`numServices` and `numEndpoints` are the *total* number of Services and Endpoints. `numNATRules` is the number of *updated* nat rules, which is not directly proportional to `numServices` and `numEndpoints`. It's more proportional to the *change* in `numServices` and `numEndpoints` since the last sync.

IOW, `numNATRules` is larger in the second sync because it had to rewrite all of the `KUBE-SVC-*` chains that used to jump to the 28 endpoints that just got deleted.

nodes.title: Fix race condition in iptables partial sync handling
nodes.body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind bug
/kind regression

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
Fixes a race condition in the iptables proxy partial sync handling; the methods that process apiserver events (`proxier.OnServiceUpdated` etc) rely on the change trackers' mutexes rather than the proxier's mutexes (since they don't use any mutable variables in the proxier), but `syncProxyRules` currently makes two separate calls into the change trackers, `PendingUpdates()` and `Update()`, so it's possible that an event could arrive between them, causing the two results to reflect inconsistent state. (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/121362#issuecomment-1840599101)

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes #121362

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
This does not add any regression test since the bug is a race condition and I don't think there's any easy way we could force it?

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Fixes a race condition in the iptables mode of kube-proxy in 1.27 and later
that could result in some updates getting lost (e.g., when a service gets a
new endpoint, the rules for the new endpoint might not be added until
much later).
```

/sig network
/priority important-soon
cc @aojea @juliantaylor

title: Request timeout not respected while listing from storage
body:
### What happened?

It is possible to issue a list request which exceeds the duration set by the request-timeout apiserver flag. The request-timeout flag does not appear to be enforced when the apiserver is decoding the response from etcd. 

Specifically, listing a large number of CRDs from etcd can result in high request latency from using json encoding compared to protobuf encoding. While overall etcd latency is low, the overall listing from storage latency may be over the 1 minute timeout, particularly if the apiserver needs to fetch multiple pages from etcd.



### What did you expect to happen?

We expected the list requests to be subject to the duration specified by the request-timeout flag when this latency is coming from the listing from storage phase of the request.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create 4000 CRs and list all the objects from etcd in 2 pages of 2000 objects. If the time to list 1 page + decode takes around 50s, listing 2 pages will result in the listing from storage phase of the request taking  around 1 minute and 40s before the request fails and the client is returned a 500 response code.

/sig api-machinery

CC: @wojtek-t @tkashem @shyamjvs

Interesting.. - do you know where exactly we stuck?

In the call to storage:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/store.go#L708

we pass the context that has timeout set, so that shouldn't hang.

OTOH, for the processing part:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/store.go#L732-L751

(a) I don't know if transformer honors the context - it probably depends on the implementation
(b) but the decoding (appendListitem) certainly isn't honoring the context

So (b) might definitely be a problem, even independently from from the transformer


So I guess what I'm saying is that if listing from etcd finishes fast but the decoding is what takes most of time, then what you described can certainly be a problem.
But is that the thing you're observing?

Yes, that is our understanding. Specifically, that the decoding which occurs in appendListItem doesn't respect the context: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/98d37747d8f874b846d86e34e4237cbeaa4c3dc9/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/store.go#L991-L1004

As a separate follow-up, it would be useful to include decoding time, or at least the overall listing from storage time, as a separate latency annotation, given the audit log entry is only capturing this latency as part of apiserver.latency.k8s.io/total.

> As a separate follow-up, it would be useful to include decoding time, or at least the overall listing from storage time, as a separate latency annotation, given the audit log entry is only capturing this latency as part of apiserver.latency.k8s.io/total.

+1. We need more granular latency tracker especially on the latency spent on decoding. Right now, it only captures etcd round trip and transformer latency.
I would be supportive for both and would be happy to review it if someone opens up a PR for it.

title: Mount point may become local without calling `NodePublishVolume` after node rebooting
body:
### What happened?

This issue is very similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117513, they have the same symptom: remote volumes of the pods are becoming local mount point after rebooting the Node. And this issue is triggered by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117513.

The difference is that in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117513, kubelet didn't call `NodeStageVolume`, so the global mount point is local, but it will still call `NodePublishVolume` for the pod to bind mount the pod volume to the global mount point. Whereas in this issue, kubelet neither call `NodeStageVolume` globally nor call `NodePublishVolume` for the pod. 

This is more harmful: After writing some data to the pod volume, pod can't be deleted because kubelet encounter `directory not empty` error while unmounting the pod volume:
 
![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/44308864/b1cc4e04-15ac-4730-a862-54eddf2a4960)


Reproduce steps:
1. Create a cluster with one Node
2. Create a deployment with **two replicas**(say `pod-1` and `pod-2`) using Non-attachable volume (for example Azurefile)
3. Shutdown the Node
4. Delete `pod-1` with option `--force` (Use force deletion to simulate the situation that mount point was left over before rebooting the Node.)
5. Bring back the Node
6. `pod-2` is always in Running state, however, after rebooting, it won't call `NodePublishVolume` and the volume it uses is local volume.

### What did you expect to happen?

`pod-2` should call `NodePublishVolume`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

As mentioned above.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
After Node rebooting and kubelet restarting, volume manger will execute [syncStates](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.27/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconstruct.go#L45): get volumes from pod dir, and reconstruct the volume and [add it to ASW and mark the volume as `volume mounted`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.27/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconstruct.go#L107) if it is not in DSW.

If multiple Pods use the same volume, and one of the pods is deleted but left over the volume in pod dir. After rebooting, only the pod deleted (that is to say, not in DSW during reconstruction) and volume left should [be added to ASW and marked as `volume mounted`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.27/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconstruct.go#L107) . 

However, since the reconstructed volume has been [added to `gvl`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.27/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconstruct.go#L86) before [judging whether it is in DSW](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.27/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconstruct.go#L87-L97), and `gvl` is a pointer variable, so the volume in DSW will also [be added to ASW and marked as `volume mounted`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.27/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconstruct.go#L107) , which makes the pods running w/o calling `NodePublishVolume`.


#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #119921

add pod volume to gvl after judging whether the volume is in DSW, that is to say, only add volumes not in DSW to gvl, so only the volumes that not in DSW will be added to ASW and marked as `volume mounted` .

@Vivekdjango you can check if hair pin mode is enabled 
https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/debug/debug-application/debug-service/#a-pod-fails-to-reach-itself-via-the-service-ip

Beside hair-pin there is another problem you can check: if you can trace traffic inside the POD, e.g. with `tcpdump`, check if packets have the POD-IP both as source and dest.

This will be the case if the source-ip (i.e. the POD-IP) is not masqueraded, and it will not work. This will _always_ happen for services with `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`, but I can see that your service doesn't use that. Another thing that may cause this sysctl net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables. Verify that it's 1, or set it with:
```
sysctl -w net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables=1
```
Another thing to test is to set `--masquerade-all` to kube-proxy. It should normally not be necessary, but worth testing.

title: Kubelet cannot finish terminating a pod that uses a PVC with volumeMode: Block when poweroff the node and then restarting the node
body:
### What happened?

A pod uses a PVC with volumeMode: Block. The block volume is backed by a block device on the node (which is created by some CSI storage providers).  If the node operating system is powered off , if the user delete the pod or the pod be eviceted by kcm, And then restarting the node, The pod would be stuck in terminating forever since Kubelet refuses to UnmapBlockVolume. kubelet  cannot delete the pod successfully.  

### What did you expect to happen?

Kubelet should be able to finish terminating a pod  

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1.Install a CSI storage provider that supports volumeMode: Block.

2.Deloy a pod that has volumeClaimTemplates with volumeMode: Block. 

```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: test-pod
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: test-pod
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: test-pod
      name: test-pod
    spec:
      containers:
      - image: nginx:1.17.9
        name: test
        volumeDevices:
        - devicePath: /dev/blk-vol-1
          name: blk-vol-1
        volumeMounts:
      volumes:
      - name: blk-vol-1
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: test-bv
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: test-bv
  namespace: default
spec:
  accessModes: [ "ReadWriteMany" ]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
  storageClassName: FILLIN
  volumeMode: Block
```
3.After pod is running ,to  power off the node
4.delete the po: kubectl delete po test-pod
5.restart the node

The pod is stuck in terminating state forever. Logs from kubelet:

nodes.title: Fix device uncertain errors on reboot
nodes.body:
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119608

The underlying reason of this issue is - when node that has pods with raw block volumes is shutdown and assuming node is shutdown for long enough time that - pods on the node get evicted (or deleted), then when the node comes back such pods will be usually stuck in terminating state. 

The reason they are stuck in terminating state is because - although volume read from pod dir gets added to ASOW in `uncertain` state, a mount may still be performed for the volume and when that happens usually mount fails and that causes volume to be updated as `unmounted` in ASOW.  When this happens, it also removes `deviceMountPath` from the volume and hence subsequent attempt to `unmap` the device fails because `deviceMountPath` is empty.


```release-note
Allow deletion of pods that use raw block volumes on node reboot
```

/sig scheduling

@alculquicondor I think sig-scheduling is handling the cronjob and job controllers, right?

/sig apps
cc @soltysh
Cronjob v2 got to stable in 1.22, so if anything, it's something more recent.

My wild guess would be that somehow kcm is reconciling all CronJobs even though they are not due for schedule.

@zigmund any chance you can look at the logs and see whether a particular cronjob with a low frequency is being reconciled continuosly?

@alculquicondor 
Checked few monthly cronjobs, don't see such problem.

But I see multiple logs about same jobs:
```
I0617 20:28:00.368553      12 job_controller.go:514] enqueueing job market-production/api-scheduler-28116868

I0617 20:28:21.066377      12 job_controller.go:514] enqueueing job market-production/api-scheduler-28116868
```

Also there are many error logs:
```
E0617 20:37:18.442053      12 cronjob_controllerv2.go:166] error syncing CronJobController market-production/api-scheduler, requeuing: Operation cannot be fulfilled on cronjobs.batch "api-scheduler": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again
```

But I also see all same logs in other healthy clusters.

@alculquicondor 

I started kcm locally for debug and that's what I found so far:
There are two cronjobs constantly readded to workqueue with negative `*requeueAfter`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.26.4/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L168-L171
Duration calculated wrongly in `getMostRecentScheduleTime`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.26.4/pkg/controller/cronjob/utils.go#L121-L143

1. Cronjob parts-panel-cronjob-products-data:
```
Schedule:                      0 16 * * *
Concurrency Policy:            Forbid
Last Schedule Time:  Fri, 16 Jun 2023 16:00:00 +0600
Active Jobs:         parts-panel-cronjob-products-data-28115160
```
Now is `2023-06-19 13:11:04`
There is 1 active long running job, started at 3 days ago, already missed some schedules, `getMostRecentScheduleTime` should return `2023-06-19 16:00:00` (in the future), but returns `2023-06-18 16:00:00` (in the past).

2. Cronjob parts-panel-cronjob-abcp-products-data:
```
Schedule:                      0 12 * * 3
Last Schedule Time:  Wed, 31 May 2023 12:00:00 +0600
Starting Deadline Seconds:     30s
Active Jobs:         <none>
```
Now is `2023-06-19 13:11:04`
Schedules at `2023-06-17 12:00:00` and `2023-06-14 12:00:00` were missed for some reason (maybe because of Starting Deadline Seconds, doesn't matters), `getMostRecentScheduleTime` should return `2023-06-21 12:00:00` (in the future), but returns `2023-06-14 12:00:00`.

Workaround - recreated these cronjobs and now kcm works fine.
Looked new code - the issue maybe already fixed in v1.27, but need to check.

@zigmund thanks for the detailed debugging.

Just for clarification `job_controller.go` is about Job, not CronJob. Jobs do need to be synced somewhat continuously while they are running.

Feel free to submit a PR if you find the fix.

/triage accepted
It happened again after another controller-manager restart.
Did you have a chance to test in 1.27?
@alculquicondor, unfortunately it's not possible to upgrade the cluster in near future.
I see. In any case @soltysh probably has more context about recent changes in CronJob that could solve the issue and can potentially be cherry-picked.
/assign

This https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/af1c9e49c498d4e984dbaa6cd65b1e86813b5ac2 seems to have fixed this problem.

I'm looking at ways to fix it. I will give some conclusions later.

> It has been **confirmed** that #110838 commit(be44d67566ac87e85d450227765cd86df1ba9bd6) corrects the error here.

We need to pay attention to the calculation method of `earliestTime` in the function `mostRecentScheduleTime` In the past, only `Status#LastScheduleTime` and `ObjectMeta#CreationTimestamp` were involved in the comparison. Now `Spec#StartingDeadlineSeconds` and `now()` will be involved in the calculation, so that the requeue time we calculate will not be a negative number. .

This is the unit test case I use for testing. You can use it for verification if you want.

https://github.com/sxllwx/kubernetes/commit/82d0a0aea6df62587857d152c78b7bc8f3201b30

There is another interesting thing here:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b46a3f887ca979b1a5d14fd39cb1af43e7e5d12d/pkg/controller/cronjob/utils.go#L140-L142

` t.UTC()` operation is **performed** on `t`, which will affect sched (I noticed that our spec does not set the time zone. I recommend setting it to `"TZ=UTC 0 12 * * 3"` Compatible with the UTC TZ of the hardcode in the code) calculates the scheduling time of the next round.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b46a3f887ca979b1a5d14fd39cb1af43e7e5d12d/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L656-L665

> I noticed that our spec does not set the time zone. I recommend setting it to `"TZ=UTC 0 12 * * 3"`

*don't* set TZ in the string schedule (that will be forbidden in future releases), set it in the cronjob spec

@sxllwx thanks for working on this

@soltysh, now that we have a crisp unit test reproducer, can we prioritize review and backport of a fix? it looks like this changed in 1.25, which is *almost* at EOL (I'm not even sure there's another patch release planned).

@sxllwx thx for your effort with reproducer 

I'll make sure to prioritize this next week on Monday to figure out possible fixes.

Indeed https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/110838 fixed a lot of issues around the calculations of time schedules, especially around its performance. Additionally PRs https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118724 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118940 and currently awaiting one https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121327 (where I've just added the test case from @sxllwx) improve both accuracy and performance. I'll check which ones we can safely backport to previous releases once the last one merges.
/assign
@soltysh nice, looking forward for patch release.

1.28 pick: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121536 - picks only #121327 
1.27 pick: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121537 - picks only #121327 
1.26 pick: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121540 - picks #110838 and #121327

All related PR's are merged, looks like we can close it now.
@soltysh thanks!

title: kubernetes-1.24.0 reproducible builds: kubelet binary varies
body:
### What happened?

While working on [reproducible builds](https://reproducible-builds.org/) for [openSUSE](https://en.opensuse.org/openSUSE:Reproducible_Builds), I found that our kubernetes1.24 package stopped to produce bit-identical results on 2 fresh builds.

The first chunk is likely just the hash of the remainder, so can be ignored.

Sources should be able to reproduce bit-identical binaries e.g. for SLSA level4

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

On Debian or openSUSE do
```bash
osc co openSUSE:Factory/kubernetes1.24 && cd $_
for i in 1 2 ; do

  --define='%source_date_epoch_from_changelog Y' \

Unfortunately not, @bmwiedemann is this something we can fix on the OBS side? If the go build timestamp (`go-build3558486601`) is the main issue here then we can approach a fix in our build pipeline.

It would be good if `/tmp/go-build$int` would not be embedded in the first place. It might be possible to replace it somehow in our builds, but all other people wanting reproducible builds, would need to replicate that.

@dims full logs from the build: https://rb.zq1.de/temp/kubernetes1.24-build-log.txt
from kubernetes-1.24.3 built 2022-08-18

@bmwiedemann can you please try setting GOCACHE=off when you run the build? 

I am suspecting that the temp directory is being generated here:
https://github.com/golang/go/blob/6d8ec893039a39f495c8139012e47754e4518b70/src/cmd/go/internal/cache/default.go#L77-L80

(or add an export in hack/lib/golang.sh for that env var)
I added `export GOCACHE=off` to [our .spec file](https://code.opensuse.org/package/kubernetes1.24/blob/6bff88072d245b1e8574f2cf672e774cc7436f79/f/kubernetes1.24.spec#_187) but still got these diffs.

So i built golang from source, peppered it with changes to track down where this is getting created and found that it is coming from:
https://github.com/golang/go/blob/c318f191e45e3496f8afe0a456337e9f76d7f7b4/src/cmd/go/internal/work/action.go#L268

I don't know yet how to fix it. will dig more when i can (travelling for the next few days)
